findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: The meat and chili on the hot holding prep table registered at temperatures below the required 135 degrees F for hot holding. The meat, when probed, registered at 100 degrees F and had been in place since 10am this day. This container was disposed of and replaced with a fresh container of meat. The chili, when probed, registered at 123 degrees F and was in place at 1pm. Using time instead of temperature, the facility must dispose of the chili in the container at 5pm to ensure its food safety integrity. If this steam table is to have continued use, then the establishment must maintain a time control log where the food is replaced every 4 hours or the steam table needs to be turned up in temperature or maintenance needs to be requested for the equipment to be fixed or replaced. The facility is going to be using a controlled substance, more than likely a pan of water, to test the temperature availability of the steam table and to better gauge if they need it fixed, replaced, or simply turned up in temperature.
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

Reference 4-501.114.

findings.comment: Observed single portion cups of chili in the top of the pan in the prep cooler that were probed at 80F. findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following non food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1)inside of dishwasher with food debris 2)outside of dishwasher with food debris and lime scale 3)milk shake toppings cooler with food debris-REPEAT 4)vents on cookline prep cooler soiled with dust 5)inside of fryers with an accumulation of grease 6)microwave soiled with food next to fryers. Clean non food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed shredded cheese inside bottom portion of prep cooler to have handle extended into cheese. Extend handle out of shredded cheese.
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
1) Observed drain by dishwasher to be soiled with an accumulation of dirt. Clean drain. 2)Observed drain underneath dishwasher to be soiled with food debris. Clean drain. 3)Observed floor underneath soda boxes to be soiled with food debris. Clean floor.-REPEAT 4)Observed floors in walk in freezer to be soiled with food debris. Clean floors of walk in freezer. 5)Observed drains below the drive through soda machine to be soiled with food debris. Clean floor.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed wall behind dish machine to be soiled with food splash and mold. Clean wall.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Observed no FSSMC on staff. Manager stated he had just expired. Provide certified food manager for all shifts.
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: There was no working thermometer in the prep cooler under the order window.   A thermometer was put in the cooler to CORRECT the violation.
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Door gaskets were torn on several refrigerators and freezers, including the door of the walk-in cooler.  (REPEAT VIOLATION)  Replace the gaskets that are torn or damaged.

750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
  (A)  top inside of the cooler (fan area) under order window  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  (B)  surfaces inside the doors of the fryers  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  (C)  French fry overhead warming unit  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  (D)  lower door seal on the freezer to the left of the fryers  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  (E)  under side of the milk dispenser-under the unit  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  (F)  black milk crates in the walk-in cooler that pans of food are stored on (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  (G) bottom inside of the 2-door freezer to the left of the milk shake station
  (H)  bottom inside of the milk shake station freezer
  (I)   door seals on refrigeration units in the vicinity of the milk shake station
  (J)  table tops on which the grills set
Clean these surfaces.

750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
(A)  Plates in the waitress station were stored uncovered and food side up.  They were put under a shelf to CORRECT the violation.
(B)  Utensils in pans on the wire rack near the waitress station (near the smoke detector annunciator panel) were stored uncovered. 
Cover the pans or put a plastic liner on the shelf above the utensils to cover them.

750-860 The food-contact surfaces of fixed equipment shall also be  protected from contamination.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
The waste baskets in both restrooms had no covers.  (REPEAT VIOLATION FOR MEN'S RESTROOM)  Provide covered waste baskets in the restrooms.

750-1110d Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors. A supply of toilet tissue shall be provided at each toilet at all times. Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.

findings.title: Containers covered, adequate number, insect and rodent proof, emptied at proper intervals, clean
findings.comment:
The lid was up on the outside grease receptacle.  It was closed to CORRECT the violation.

750-1130a Garbage and refuse shall be kept in durable easily cleanable, insect-proof, and rodent-proof containers.

findings.title: Outside storage area clean, enclosure properly constructed
findings.comment:
The concrete pad near the grease dumpster outside was soiled with grease  (REPEAT VIOLATION)   Clean the pad.

750-1140c Outside storage areas shall be kept clean.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
The following floors were soiled:
  (A)  under the shelving in the walk-in freezer (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  (B)  under the dish machine up close to the wall  (REPEAT VIOLATION), and under all the trays in the dish room next to the walls.
  (C)  corner of the dish room to the right of the dish machine  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  (D)  floor and green plastic risers that the soda lines go in to the right of the walk-in cooler door  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  (E)  threshold of the back exterior door  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  (F)  around the soda  conduit coming up out of the floor under the soda dispenser at the drive-up window  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  (G) floor next to the wall under several pieces of equipment on the cook line  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  (H)  floor drains throughout the kitchen and dish room
Clean the floors and the drains.

750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
The following walls and ceilings were soiled:
  (A)  The vent and adjacent surfaces in the hood over the dish machine were soiled.  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  (B)  The wall behind the dish machine was soiled.  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
  (C)  The wall around the lower base of the mop sink
  (D)  The vent in the ceiling above the milk shake station
Clean the walls and ceiling surfaces.

750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
One mop was stored with its head in the mop sink because the wall holder was not tight enough to hold the wet mop.  Store the mop out of the sink so it will drain and dry properly.

750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
(A) Hot dogs were 52 degrees in the open cooler to the right of the grills.  The time the hotdogs had been out of temperature was unknown.  They were discarded to CORRECT. the violation.       (B) Hamburger, sausage, cheese, and bacon in the open cooler to the left of the grills were 46-51 degrees.  The time the food had been out of temperature was unknown.  The food was discarded to CORRECT the violation.

750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Containers of baked beans in a drawer warmer to the right of the order counter were 122 degrees.  They were discarded to CORRECT the violation.

750-250  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 135°F or above  while on display and service.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment:
There were no thermometers in the following units:        (A) walk-in freezer (the electronic thermometer was not working) ,        (B) drawer warmer on cook line where ready-to-serve baked beans are kept.       (C) freezer to the left of the fryers   (REPEAT VIOLATION)        (D) milk dispenser  (REPEAT VIOLATION)
Put thermometers in these units.    750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer.      750.150(a) All hot units that contain potentially hazardous foods shall contain  a conspicuously placed thermometer.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Raw beef patties were stored above buns and raw bacon was stored above strawberries in the walk-in freezer.  The beef patties and bacon were placed in different location to avoid the potential for cross contamination to CORRECT the violation.

750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
(A) The drive-up window ice bin lid was open.  Close the lid.       (B) The ice cream was uncovered in the milkshake station.   Cover the ice cream.         (C) Several containers of food in coolers were not covered.   Keep covers on all food in refrigerators and freezers.         (D) There were boxes of food on the floor of the walk-in freezer.  Elevate the food at least 6 inches off the floor.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.   750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment:
A plastic single use cup was used as a scoop in the Parmesan cheese in the waitress station glass front cooler.  Remove the cup and sue a scoop with a handle and store it with the handle up out of the food.

750-160 Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
The ice scoop handle in the drive-up area ice bin was laying in the ice.  Store the scoop so the handle is sticking up out of the ice.

750-290 Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
A person drink was stored on a shelf above the caramel and hot fudge dispenser in the drive up window area.  The drink was moved to CORRECT the violation.

750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
The door gaskets on the freezer near the drive-up window (below the warming unit)  are torn.  Replace the gaskets.

750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
A wet wiping cloth in the waitress station was not stored in a bucket of sanitizer.  Store the cloths in buckets of sanitizer between uses.

750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: The following food contact surfaces were soiled:          (A) soda nozzles and adjacent surfaces on dispenser in waitress station,   (B) soda nozzles on dispenser at the drive-up window,      (C) white baffle inside the ice machine,         (D) inside and outside the microwave above the steam table,        (E) underside of shelf above the steam table,       (F) top inside of freezer to the right of the grills (condensation),      Clean and sanitize these surfaces.    750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
See page 2, "GENERAL COMMENTS" for violations.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.
Clean the surfaces listed on page 2.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
(A) Plates were stored food side up in the chili 5-way station.  They were inverted to CORRECT the violation.  
(B) Bowls were stored food side up in the waitress station.  Store them inverted or covered.

750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: (A) Coffee filters were stored unprotected in the waitress station.          (B) Cup lids were stored food side up in (1) the waitress station, (2) milkshake station, and (3) at the drive-up window.           (C) Forks in the black plastic organizer behind the front counter were stored with their handles and eating ends inter-mixed.        (D) Boxes of cups were stored on the floor of the dry goods storage room.     750.880  Store the coffee filters in closed containers or bags.  Store the cup lids inverted or covered.  Arrange the forks so they are all in one direction. elevate the boxes of cups at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
(A) The waste baskets in the men's bathroom had no covers.  Provide covers for the wastebaskets.
(B) There was no soap and paper towels at the waitress station handsink.  Provide both at the sink.

750-1110d Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials in toilet facilities.
750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Outside storage area clean, enclosure properly constructed
findings.comment:
The concrete pad and surrounding grassy area around the outside dumpster was littered with debris and the concrete pad is soiled.   Remove the litter and clean the concrete pad.   (REPEAT VIOLATION)

750-1140c Outside storage areas shall be kept clean.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
The back door is self-closing and tight fitting but was left cracked open twice while employees stepped outside for a break.  The door was closed each time to CORRECT the violation.  Keep the door closed at all times.  Use the door bell to get back in.

750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
See page 2, "GENERAL COMMENTS" for violations.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. 
Clean the floor surfaces listed on page 2.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
(A) The vent and adjacent surfaces in the hood over the dish machine were soiled.
(B) The wall behind the dish machine and to the right of it were soiled.   (REPEAT VIOLATION)
(C) The wall below the tray where dirty dishes are stored in the dish room was soiled.  

Clean these walls.      750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
A spray can of Raid bug spray and an empty spray bottle of cleaner was stored on a shelf in the dish washing area above clean plates.  Both containers were put on the bottom shelf below any equipment to CORRECT the violation.

750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food and food utensils) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
There was no certified Food Service Sanitation Manager on duty.   Have a certified food manager on duty any time potentially hazardous food is being handled.

750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.
